transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-10-07
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Horizon Procurement), Carlos Mendez (Horizon Security), Ellen Park (Horizon Legal), Samir Patel (Horizon CTO)

SUMMARY:
Quick kickoff to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, KMS/HSM requirements, and next milestones to unblock procurement. Also to triage whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for PHI-sensitive workloads.

TOPICS:
- MSA/DPA high level redline review
- SLA targets and uptime/latency expectations
- KMS/HSM integration, key custody and rotation
- Data residency and export-control flags
- Pricing approvals and billing cadence
- Next steps and timelines

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, um, appreciate the time. quick intro from our side — i'm maya, i'll be leading commercial and onboarding. liam from infra will do the technical bits. ..
[00:18] Priya Nair: thanks maya. we're running this intake for horizon, we need the procurement checklist and we have a tentative Q4 go-live window, subject to legal sign off and KMS approval. so today's about alignment.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: hey all, yeah i'll try to keep it focused — we've onboarded similar health customers, so i can go through our typical private deployment gating and the KMS flow. quick question, are you planning to keep keys on-prem or use cloud HSMs?
[00:50] Samir Patel: prefer customer-managed HSM / HSM in our cloud account, we can't put keys in vendor-managed KMS, part of our policy — especially for PHI. also data residency — east-usa only.
[01:06] Carlos Mendez: and to add, we need audit trails for key usage, key rotation logs and proof of separation of duties. SOC 2 plus ISO would be nice to have.
[01:20] Ellen Park: from legal: MSA/DPA redlines — we have standard healthcare addendum, we will push our redlines. we need to understand what Redwood's liability caps look like and data return/destruction clauses.
[01:36] Maya Chen: totally, thanks. high-level on the DPA — we previously shared our standard DPA (link: /redwood/dpa-v3.pdf). i'll follow up with a redline that highlights endpoints for on-prem and private deployments. liability caps are typically negotiated at enterprise tier, we can note that for your procurement team.
[01:55] Priya Nair: pricing perspective — how does billing work for dedicated vs private? do we still get usage-based billing on private or is it reserved commit?
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: good q. dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; private deployments are a separate licensing model — there is a platform fee plus either a committed capacity or bring-your-own infra billing depending on the package. we can map to your expected qps and throughput and produce TCO numbers.
[02:28] Samir Patel: we need baseline latency numbers for 2k token sequences. can you share perf numbers for nvidia h100 and a quantized fp16 path?
[02:42] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll share perf spreadsheet. quick note: sequence length and KV cache usage matter — the numbers differ if you use continuous chat or short completions. i'll include a range and the kernel/compilation flags we used.
[03:00] Carlos Mendez: back to security — KMS integration, can you support our BYOK via cloud HSM (we use Azure Key Vault HSM, and some workloads on GCP KMS)? also require in-transit encryption to mutual TLS with client certs.
[03:18] Maya Chen: we do support BYOK for Private and Dedicated; hosted API supports customer-managed keys via entitlements but that is more limited. mutual TLS for private is supported — i'll get liam to capture the exact cert flow.
[03:33] Ellen Park: for DPA, we also need subprocessor lists and SOC 2 audit reports. do you have a page we can link to?
[03:42] Maya Chen: yes, security portal — i'll send the link after the call. (note: /redwood/security/soc2-report) but we can also provide an ATO package under NDA for deeper reviews.
[03:55] Priya Nair: timeline wise, procurement wants costs and DPA redlines by Oct 12 to make next committee on Oct 15. is that feasible?
[04:06] Maya Chen: yes we can aim for that. liam — ok to prepare the perf and private deployment checklist by Oct 18?
[04:14] Liam O'Connor: yes that's fine.
[04:20] [15:00 - PARAPHRASE SKIP - mid call technical deep dive and some crosstalk]
[20:45] Liam O'Connor: i'm recording a few gotchas: 1) KV cache persistence across restarts — we can persist in a secure object store; 2) data purge — we have a configurable retention policy; 3) quantization affects perf but may impact emergent behavior slightly — we'll flag the evals.
[21:03] Carlos Mendez: on audit logging, we need per-request token-level traces for debugging, but those must be redacted for PHI. is that supported?
[21:18] Liam O'Connor: yes, we can provide token/trace level logs to your security team behind an access control gate; we also support scramble/redaction and filtered logs for production.
[21:32] Ellen Park: legal question — data deletion clause. how soon after contract termination do you guarantee data erasure and do you provide cert of destruction?
[21:45] Maya Chen: standard is 90 days for hosted with cert on request; for private we can do immediate destruction since data is in customer account — we'll add language for certified deletion for private deployments.
[22:00] Priya Nair: SLA specifics — our apps require 99.95% uptime for inference API and P99 latency under 200ms for short completions. can you meet that with your dedicated pools?
[22:16] Liam O'Connor: 99.95% is in tiered SLAs for dedicated — depends on region and redundancy. p99 200ms for small generations is achievable on Dedicated with autoscale policies, but for long sequences and high concurrency we should design capacity plans.
[22:35] Samir Patel: what's fall-over behavior? if dedicated capacity is exhausted, do you fail open to a cheaper hosted model? data residency concerns.
[22:46] Maya Chen: we have routing policies: you can set hard constraints to prevent routing off-region/off-tier. fallback to hosted is optional; for Horizon we recommend disabled fallback to hosted if regs prohibit it.
[23:00] Carlos Mendez: any controls on tokenization logs? we need to ensure PHI doesn't show up in logs.
[23:09] Liam O'Connor: we support token-level redaction and a privacy layer that strips payloads at the edge, but config needs to be set prior to onboarding.
[23:25] Ellen Park: MSA liability cap — our counsel will propose a multiple of fees. are there precedents for raising caps for healthcare?
[23:40] Maya Chen: yes, at enterprise tier we've flexed caps with insurance proofs; we can provide references and insurance certificate on request.
[23:52] Priya Nair: procurement — what supporting docs for pricing approvals do you need? forecast, TCO, SLA impact on cost?
[24:05] Maya Chen: we'll provide a pricing packet with tiered options: hosted per-token, dedicated commit, private license + infra estimates. we'll add a simple TCO sheet matching your expected qps and retention.
[24:20] [minor audio glitch]
[29:10] Liam O'Connor: technical note: for Azure HSM integration we need a short-lived service principal and an approval flow; for GCP KMS there's an IAM mapping. we'll include step-by-step in the KMS handoff doc.
[29:30] Carlos Mendez: good. can you also indicate if Redwood supports hardware attestation or TPM-based keys for private air-gapped installs?
[29:40] Liam O'Connor: yes, for on-prem installs we support HSM-backed keys and can do attestation flows; we may need some professional services to enable this the first time.
[29:55] Samir Patel: will there be any outbound data transfers? some regulators want no cross-border calls.
[30:04] Maya Chen: routing policies can pin to region; for private it remains on your network, so no cross border. we'll document the egress map.
[30:20] Ellen Park: legal — we have a carve-out for export control data; need clarity on subprocessors that are outside the US.
[30:33] Maya Chen: i'll include the subprocessor sheet and we can mark countries flagged by your legal team.
[30:45] Priya Nair: ok around next steps, procurement wants a short one-pager summarizing the differences between dedicated vs private including price bands and KMS patterns.
[30:58] Maya Chen: noted; we'll produce that. action items on both sides.
[31:10] [end of main Q&A; wrap-up]
[31:20] Maya Chen: recap — redwood to share redlined DPA, SOC 2 proof, pricing/TCO, KMS integration notes by Oct 12-18 window. horizon to provide list of restricted regions and required legal redlines by Oct 14. we'll schedule a technical deep dive the week of Oct 19. anything else?
[31:45] Priya Nair: that's it from procurement. thanks.
[31:50] Carlos Mendez: sounds good, i'll follow up on the HSM specifics.
[31:55] Ellen Park: i'll get legal redlines over.
[32:00] Samir Patel: thanks everyone.

CLOSING NOTES:
Links shared: Redlined DPA template (internal link), SOC 2 portal, Private deployment checklist (to follow), Perf spreadsheet (to follow)

ACTION ITEMS (as captured):
- Maya Chen: share redlined DPA and security links by 2026-10-12
- Liam O'Connor: perf baseline and private deployment checklist by 2026-10-18
- Carlos Mendez: provide HSM/rotation policy and restricted countries list by 2026-10-14

END OF TRANSCRIPT
